title: Generics
explain: Generics let a class or method work with many types while the compiler still checks them. A `List<String>` can hold only strings, so you don't need casts when you read from it. A bounded type like `<T extends Comparable<T>>` limits which types are allowed.
exercise: Write a generic `swap` method that exchanges two elements of a `List<T>`.
tip: Generics are erased at runtime, so you can't write `new T()` or `instanceof List<String>`. Pass a `Class<T>` or a supplier when you need that.
